parameters.text:
=Hi, I am Handshake AI. Every handshake becomes a follow-up.

Here is everything I can do:

CAPTURE SOMEONE YOU JUST MET
- Photo of their business card, badge or LinkedIn profile (several cards in one photo work too)
- Voice note: "Just met Sara, CTO at Acme, wants help automating invoices..."
- Quick text with whatever you remember
I research them, give them a lead score from 0 to 100, draft a personal follow-up in Gmail, save them in your sheet and remind you to send it. Same person twice? I update them instead of adding a duplicate.

ON EACH CONTACT CARD
- Show email / Send email / Rewrite (shorter, more formal, Italian, Arabic)
- Snooze 3 days / LinkedIn note / Not relevant
- WhatsApp (message ready to send) / LinkedIn / Save to phone
- Reply to a card with text to change anything, or with a photo to save their picture

COMMANDS
/people - everyone you met at an event, e.g. /people Web Summit
/search - find people by skill or interest, e.g. /search flutter
/top - your 5 best open leads by score
/match - introductions worth making between people you know
/nudges - people you have not talked to in 30 days, with a reason and a message
/stats - results of an event
/edit - change someone you already saved, e.g. /edit Sara phone +39 333 123 4567
/ask - ask about your network, e.g. /ask who should I follow up with?
/recap - everyone you met today, send all drafts at once
/event - set the event, e.g. /event Web Summit Lisbon
/help - this guide

Every morning at 9 I remind you about follow-ups and people you have gone quiet with. Every Sunday at 6pm I suggest introductions.

Use the buttons below the keyboard for quick access.

Your chat ID: {{ String(($json.chatId) ?? '').replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>') }}

Rules:
- Write in {{ $('Config').first().json.emailLanguage }}. Tone: {{ $('Config').first().json.tone }}.
- Under 120 words, plain text, no markdown, no em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well'.
- Open with a specific detail from the conversation notes. If there are no notes, mention the event and something concrete about their company.

parameters.content:
# Handshake AI
### Every handshake becomes a follow-up
Meet someone, then send the bot their business card, a voice note, a quick text or a LinkedIn screenshot. A minute later they are researched, scored and saved in Google Sheets, and a personal follow-up is waiting in your Gmail drafts.

### What it does
- **Capture**: card photos (several cards in one photo), voice notes, text, LinkedIn screenshots
- **Research and write**: web research, lead score, follow-up draft, no duplicates
- **Buttons** under every contact: send, rewrite, snooze, LinkedIn note, WhatsApp, save to phone
- **Ask your network**: /ask, /search, /people, /top, /stats
- **Stay in touch**: /recap, morning reminders, /nudges, weekly /match intros
- **Edit** by replying to a contact card, or reply with a photo to add their picture

### Setup
1. Create a bot with @BotFather and add the token as a Telegram credential.
2. Connect OpenAI, Gmail and Google Sheets. For voice notes, add a free Groq API key as a Header Auth credential (name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_KEY`) on **Transcribe voice note**.
   Models are set to gpt-4.1-mini; any OpenAI model that can read images and search the web works.
3. Create a Google Sheet with a tab named **Contacts** and `id` in cell A1. The other columns are added on the first save.
4. Fill in the **Config** node, and set the same time zone in Workflow settings so the 9:00 and Sunday runs fire at your local time.
5. Activate, send /start to the bot and paste the chat ID at the end of its reply into allowedChatId. Until you do, the bot only replies with its guide.

### How to read this canvas
Every message comes in on the left, is sorted by type, and runs one numbered section on the right. Each section has its own note.

values.content:
You research a professional contact someone just met, using web search. Look for their public professional footprint: LinkedIn profile, company website, personal site or blog, talks, articles, GitHub, podcasts and company news.

If from_linkedin is true, the contact was captured from a screenshot of their LinkedIn profile: finding their exact public LinkedIn profile URL (linkedin.com/in/...) is your top priority. Search for their name together with their headline, company and location, and put the URL in linkedin_url when the name and headline or company match.

Rules:
- Only public, professional information. Never include home addresses, family, health, private phone numbers or anything personal.
- Make sure every result is about the same person: match name plus company, role or location. If you can't confirm it, leave the field empty and set confidence to low.
- Never invent facts. Use empty strings or empty arrays when nothing is found.

=Research this person:
{{ JSON.stringify($json, null, 2) }}

parameters.content:
## 1. Capture a new contact
**Photo**: the AI reads the business card, badge or LinkedIn screenshot. Several cards in one photo? Each card runs on its own.
**Voice note**: Groq turns it into text first.
**Text**: goes straight to the AI.
All three end in **Clean up contact**, one tidy record, and you get an instant "Got it".

## 2. Research, write and save
Checks if this person is already saved, so nobody is added twice. Researches them online, gives a lead score from 0 to 100 and writes a short, personal follow-up.
With an email address, the follow-up becomes a Gmail draft (replacing any older draft). The contact is saved to Google Sheets and you get a summary card with buttons, with their photo if you added one.

## 3. Edit a contact
**Reply to a contact card** with a change, like "phone +39 333 1234567". The AI works out what changed and updates that row.
**/edit name change** finds the person by name. One match is edited, several give you buttons to pick, none creates nothing.
**Reply to a contact card with a photo** to save it as their picture.

## 4. Buttons under each contact card
Every button tap lands here. **Plan button action** works out which button and which contact, then **Which button?** runs it:
send the email now, change the status (snooze, not relevant, meeting booked), show the draft, rewrite it (shorter, more formal, Italian, Arabic), write a LinkedIn note, or make a contact file to save on your phone. WhatsApp and LinkedIn buttons are plain links and need no steps.

## 5. Ask your network
**/ask** or **/search**: the AI answers from your sheet, then sends photos of the people it found.
**/people [event]**: everyone you met at an event, newest first.
**/top**: your 5 best open leads.
**/stats [event]**: how an event went.

## 6. Daily recap
**/recap** lists everyone you met today. If drafts are waiting, it adds a **Send all drafts** button: one tap sends every Gmail draft and marks those contacts as sent.

## 7. Reminders and nudges
**Every morning at 9** (your time zone): follow-ups that are due today, plus people you have gone quiet with.
**/nudges [days]**: people you have not talked to in a while, each with a short check-in message you can send.

## 8. Matchmaker
**/match**, and every Sunday at 18:00: the AI looks for pairs of your contacts who should meet and explains why.
Tap **Write intro** and one Gmail draft is saved, addressed to both of them.

## 9. Settings and help
**/event name** sets the event for new contacts.
Anyone not in allowedChatId gets a polite "private assistant" reply.
**/start**, **/help** or any unknown /command shows the help guide (with your chat ID).

## 0. Front door
Four ways in: a **Telegram message**, the **9:00 morning** run, the **Sunday 18:00** matchmaker run, and the workflow **calling itself** once per card when a photo holds several cards.
**Route message** works out what came in (photo, voice, text, command, button tap or reply) and checks the sender is allowed. **Route by message type** sends it to the matching section on the right.

### Start here
Fill in **Config**: your name, role, offer, event, tone, time zone and Google Sheet ID.
Activate, then send /start to your bot: the reply ends with your chat ID. Paste it into **allowedChatId**. Until then the bot only answers with that guide and sends no reminders. Add more IDs with commas to let others in; the first ID is the owner (gets reminders, can send emails).
